evidence_checks.title: Hermann Hauke, BSB Latin fragments catalogue I (1994), pp. 91 and 187
evidence_checks.inspection: Complete 477-page generated PDF acquired. Printed pp. 91 and 187 original images directly inspected. Clm 29270(8 is a ninth-century Salzburg Gospel fragment collection; Clm 29303(1 is a sixth-century northern Italian Comes duplex surviving as two strips. The old Clm 29155 c alias is not unique enough to merge the records.
evidence_checks.limitations: Catalogue identity and contents evidence, not independent palaeographic dating, Ravenna copying, local use or complete annual-book evidence.

evidence_checks.title: BSB Clm 29270(8, current 16-canvas Gospel-fragment digitization
evidence_checks.inspection: Complete IIIF manifest and all 16 full-resolution canvases acquired. Canvas 1 shelfmark, canvas 3 identification slip and canvas 7 Mark 14 Gospel narrative directly inspected. Manifest assigns first-half ninth-century Salzburg origin and PDM images. This is the object linked by Usuarium 6411, not the CLA IX 1334 lectionary strips. Retention and interpretation qualification after independent review: the object-level PDM does not clear modern calibration canvas1, which is excluded from public retention. Auxiliary canvases2–5 and14 are short identification metadata. Canvas4 retains an older tentative VIII-century / John XII25–41 label, distinct from the current first-half ninth-century Salzburg assignment; no single-codex identity for every label is inferred.
evidence_checks.limitations: Only canvases 1, 3 and 7 directly viewed; no full literal Gospel collation. The Last Supper narrative is not a Canon or Eucharistic prayer. Fifteen image canvases are proposed retained, distinguished by content; canvas1 is private. All16 were acquired. Older labels are not harmonized with current dating.

evidence_checks.title: Anthony Ward, Entry-point to the Rotulus of Ravenna, Notitiae 25/273 (1989), pp. 351–382
evidence_checks.inspection: Whole 80-page issue acquired; pp. 351–352 / PDF pp. 43–44 directly image inspected. Ward numbers a 42-text collection but omits unusably fragmentary no. 1 from his practical reconstruction and combines nos. 40/41; his orthography and concordance are adapted. Modern liturgical reuse is reported by the author.
evidence_checks.limitations: No diplomatic manuscript collation, 42-complete-prayer claim, annual Mass-book extent or ancient Ravenna local-use inference.

evidence_checks.title: Ravenna-Cervia official diocesan Proper announcement, 18 October 2025
evidence_checks.inspection: Complete official HTML and published cover image inspected. The diocese reports a renewed volume of Mass formularies and readings for its local saints and blesseds entering force on 23 July, as an appendix to the Roman Missal. The body does not state the year; publication metadata is 18 October 2025.
evidence_checks.limitations: Only an announcement and cover were acquired. No full book, decree or text collation. This narrow modern local-use report does not establish the ancient fragments as local Ravenna books.

uses.actual_modern_scope: The official news source reports a diocesan Proper entering force, but its body omits the year and no book/decree was acquired. It is separate from ancient reception.

versions.date: Late-sixth-century catalogue interpretation: ELMSS 576–600; Hauke sixth century; Usuarium 575–600 with a conflicting current shelfmark/link
versions.source_locus: Hauke 1994 printed p. 187 versus p. 91; ELMSS 1835 / CLA IX 1334 complete delivered sample; Usuarium 6411 card and its linked BSB bsb00001710.
